items.summary: The Boston Celtics (11-6) visit the Washington Wizards (7-11) on Tuesday night at Capital One Arena, with the teams arriving in sharply contrasting form…but not the form their records would suggest. items.title: Nuggets’ Julian Strawther Cleared For Season Debut
items.summary: No players are listed on the Nuggets’ latest injury report (Twitter link), which means that Julian Strawther will be available for the first time this season when the Mavericks visit Denver on Tuesday. Strawther suffered a left knee injury during the Nuggets’ preseason game on October 14 and was diagnosed with a sprain two days left after undergoing imaging. The 6’6″ guard was ruled out for at least six weeks, but he’ll beat that projected timeline, having been cleared to make his season debut roughly five-and-a-half weeks after the team made that announcement. The 29th overall pick in the 2023 draft, Strawther appeared in 172 regular season games for Denver during his first three NBA seasons, averaging 7.1 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 1.1 assists in 16.2 minutes per contest, with a .429/.346/.801 shooting line. items.title: Pacers Notes: Nesmith, McConnell, Smith, Shooting, More
items.summary: Small forward Aaron Nesmith converted 39.6% of his three-point attempts in his first four years with the Pacers, but he’s mired in a brutal slump to open his fifth season in Indiana. He has gone 0-for-13 from long distance over his last four games, dropping his three-point percentage to 26.3% through 15 appearances. Nesmith, who’s owed about $51.4MM over the next three seasons, will miss Monday’s game against Oklahoma City due to right foot soreness, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports, noting that foot and ankle problems have plagued the 27-year-old for years (All Twitter links). Head coach Rick Carlisle said pregame that Nesmith is “banged up” with foot, ankle and knee injuries, Dopirak adds, but the team hopes he won’t be out long. items.title: Wizards Notes: Keefe, Middleton, George, Young, Carrington
items.summary: After a 4-3 start, the Wizards lost eight straight games, putting increased scrutiny on head coach Brian Keefe, as Josh Robbins and David Aldridge of The Athletic (free link) wrote last week. In another story for The Athletic (free link), Robbins cites two league sources who said Keefe’s job may have been in jeopardy had the skid continued. However, the Wizards have now won three straight games, with the latest being a wire-to-wire 20-point victory over Orlando on Sunday, which has “cooled Keefe’s hot seat for now,” per Robbins. Veteran wing Khris Middleton helped organize a players-only meeting when the losing streak hit eight games and told his teammates to maintain communication, play more physically, and “show a little bit more fight,” according to fourth-year forward Bilal Coulibaly. items.title: Cameron Boozer Out At Least Four Weeks With Ankle Injury
items.summary: Rookie forward Cameron Boozer, the third overall pick in the 2026 draft, will miss at least four weeks after testing revealed a moderate-grade medial sprain of his right ankle, the Grizzlies announced (via Twitter). According to Michael Wallace of Grind City Media (Twitter link), Memphis is taking “extreme precaution” in its approach to Boozer’s injury, which occurred in the third quarter of Thursday’s win over Golden State. The former Duke star is traveling with the Grizzlies on their road trip, Wallace adds. It’s a tough blow for Boozer, an early contender for Rookie of the Year, and for the Grizzlies, who are already missing forwards GG Jackson II (foot fracture/surgery) and Jerami Grant (calf strain). Guard Scotty Pippen Jr. (herniated disc) remains sidelined as well. The Grizzlies have been ravaged by injuries over the past couple years, a trend that seems to be continuing in…

items.title: Bulls Notes: Splitter, Giddey, Buzelis, Hield, Smith
items.summary: The Bulls’ rocky season continued on Friday with a close loss to Washington in which starters Josh Giddey and Matas Buzelis were benched for the final 7:59 of the fourth quarter. As Julia Poe of The Chicago Tribune writes, both players were once viewed as cornerstone pieces for the Bulls, but it’s no longer clear if that’s the case under a new front office led by Bryson Graham and a new head coach in Tiago Splitter. Splitter had a simple and incisive explanation for his decision afterward, telling reporters, “I thought they didn’t have a good game.” While Splitter has said he has no plans to remove either player from the starting five, it’s apparent neither is a lock to be part of closing lineups after multiple late-game benchings, Poe notes. items.summary: November 23: Vincent’s contract with Sacramento is official, the team announced today (link to press release). items.title: Nikola Jokic, Anthony Davis Named Players Of The Week
items.summary: Nuggets center Nikola Jokic is the Western Conference Player of the Week, according to the NBA (Twitter link), with Wizards big man Anthony Davis claiming the award in the East. Jokic and Davis won for games played from Nov. 16 – 22 (Week 5 of the regular season). After a relatively slow start to the season by his lofty standards, three-time MVP Jokic averaged 28.8 points, 12.0 rebounds and 9.5 assists on .600/.421/.895 shooting last week. Denver went 3-1 in those games, with a loss to Phoenix followed by wins against Boston, Houston and Chicago. Davis helped Washington go 3-1 last week, including three straight wins that snapped an eight-game losing streak. The 10-time All-Star forward/center averaged 26.5 PPG, 9.0 RPG, 1.5 APG, 1.3 BPG and 1.0 SPG on .586/.444/.714 shooting in a loss to Memphis and wins over Toronto, Chicago and Orlando.
